_README: SCENE GEOMETRY -- AUTHORED BY HAND. Nothing here is guessed or inferred.
Every geometric value below is null on purpose. The starter kit promised a
samples/camera.md describing the scene; it does not exist, so this file is
the only description of the scene the pipeline has.
2. open tools/annotate.html in a browser (no install, runs from file://),
load that frame, draw every shape, press Download zones.json, and move
the downloaded file over this one.
Look at check.png. Do not trust this file until you have.
Fails loudly while any null remains. The pipeline runs this on load.
COORDINATES are pixels in the frame named by authored_against, origin at
the TOP-LEFT, x right, y DOWN. If you re-author against a different
resolution, update authored_against and the loader will rescale.

authored_against._draw: Fill from the frame you annotated. The loader rescales every coordinate by image_width/height if the video resolution differs.

carriageway._draw: The drivable road surface as one polygon: kerb to kerb, INCLUDING the intersection box, EXCLUDING pavements, verges and parking bays. Anything outside this is not road, so a pedestrian here is on the carriageway. Trace it generously around the far end where perspective compresses it -- a few pixels there is many metres.

lanes._draw: One polygon per lane of travel, from the frame edge (or the stop line) to where the lane leaves the frame. Lanes must not overlap; together they should tile the carriageway. Add one entry per lane -- duplicate this block.
lanes._draw_direction: Draw an ARROW along the lane, in the direction traffic legally flows. Two points: tail then head. The loader turns this into a unit vector; a track whose heading differs from it by more than the wrong_way threshold is driving against traffic.
lanes._permitted: Which manoeuvres are legal FROM this lane. Any of: through, left, right, u_turn. Read the painted arrows on the road surface. An empty list means unknown, not 'none'.
lanes._governed: id of the stop_lines entry this lane must stop at, or null if this lane has no stop line in frame.

stop_lines._draw: The painted transverse bar vehicles must stop behind. Two points, LEFT-TO-RIGHT AS SEEN BY THE APPROACHING DRIVER. The orientation fixes the sign of the crossing test, so do not reverse it later.
stop_lines._approach: Which signed side approaching vehicles start on, +1 or -1, per src.geometry.side_of_line with the segment as authored. annotate.html computes this for you: after the two bar clicks, click once where a waiting car would sit.

crossings._draw: The pedestrian crossing surface (zebra bars or the marked corridor) as a polygon. A pedestrian inside this is NOT jaywalking; a vehicle inside it while a pedestrian is on it is failure_to_yield.

signal_queue_zones._draw: Where vehicles legitimately sit still waiting for a green: roughly the last few car lengths before each stop line. stopped_vehicle is suppressed inside this polygon, otherwise every red phase becomes a false positive. Err on the LARGE side -- a missed stopped_vehicle costs one FN, a queue full of them costs many FPs.

traffic_lights._draw: Tight box around the signal head's lamps only, as [x1, y1, x2, y2]. Exclude the housing and sky. If no signal is visible in frame, leave this list EMPTY -- do not invent one; the red_light and stop_line rules will then have to infer phase from traffic behaviour instead.

lane_markings._draw: Longitudinal painted lines, as a two-point segment each. Split a line into several entries where its style changes. style must be one of: solid, dashed, double_solid. Only crossing a solid or double_solid is solid_line_crossing.

notes: Free text: anything about the scene a rule author needs and cannot see from the geometry alone (e.g. 'the far approach is one-way', 'the signal is out of frame to the left').
